title: heartbeat-sampler-sweep-notes-marina
content:
Goal:
- quick exploratory sweep of heartbeat-based pacing (local "tick" every X ms) to dampen microbursts and reduce p99 amplification during short spikes. want a cheap mitigation that doesn't require global queue re-architecture.

Test summary (informal):
- harness: synthetic client emulating real product trace (zipf-ish user session arrivals), but intentionally inject short 1-3s microbursts (50–200 qps above baseline).
- target model: llama-2-7b-quant (local dev flavor), seq=512, typical token output ~40 tokens.
- HW: single dedicated GPU (A10G) on dev cluster (shared pool), 8 worker threads in runtime, kv cache warm for steady-state.
- baseline: no heartbeat/pacing, dynamic batching on with 20ms batch timeout, max batch size 32.

Sweep knobs:
- heartbeat interval: [10ms, 25ms, 50ms, 100ms]
- heartbeat strategy: soft-delay (hold short window before enqueuing), immediate-priority-resume (drops into fast lane after quiet period), aggregate-window (coalesce arrivals into small buckets)
- aggressive-throttle: on|off (boolean switch to simulate quick backoff)

Metrics captured (per-run):
- p50/p90/p95/p99 latency (server-side token generation latency)
- observed qps during burst windows
- batch size distribution
- KV-cache hit rate
- request drops / tail-off events

Representative run data (abbrev; numbers are median-of-3 runs, small harness variance):
1) baseline (no heartbeat) -- burst +50 qps for 2s:
   p50: 56ms, p90: 140ms, p95: 220ms, p99: 520ms
   avg batch size: 15, kv-hit: 0.92, observed peak qps: 250
   notes: clear p99 spikes at burst onset; many small batches while workers ramp.

2) heartbeat=50ms, soft-delay:
   p50: 64ms, p90: 120ms, p95: 170ms, p99: 260ms
   avg batch size: 20, kv-hit: 0.90, observed peak qps: 240
   notes: p99 reduced ~2x vs baseline; slight p50 increase (added delay). good tradeoff for interactive apps.

3) heartbeat=25ms, aggregate-window:
   p50: 70ms, p90: 110ms, p95: 150ms, p99: 210ms
   avg batch size: 23, kv-hit: 0.88, observed peak qps: 235
   notes: better smoothing; lower p95/p99. small throughput loss due to coalescing but acceptable.

4) heartbeat=10ms, immediate-priority-resume + aggressive-throttle=on:
   p50: 48ms, p90: 100ms, p95: 190ms, p99: 470ms
   avg batch size: 14, kv-hit: 0.93, observed peak qps: 255
   notes: fast resume keeps p50 small but p99 still bad — likely due to contention when throttle flips back and forth (thrashing).

Observations / hypotheses:
- middle-range heartbeat (25-50ms) seems to give best p99 reduction without large p50 penalty.
- aggregate-window strategies that intentionally coalesce arrivals into micro-batches increase batch size and reduce tail, at cost of added latency for very low qps clients.
- immediate-resume heuristics can undo benefits by creating oscillation (rapid enter/exit), especially when aggressive throttle is toggled; need hysteresis.
- kv-cache hit rate dips slightly with larger coalescing — maybe because session affinity windows misaligned; investigate sticky-worker assignment / cache TTL interplay.

Quick ASCII sparkline (p99 across knobs, lower is better):
- baseline:    ▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇ (520)
- hb=50 soft:  ▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇    (260)
- hb=25 agg:   ▇▇▇▇▇▇      (210)
- hb=10 resume:▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇  (470)

Anomalies spotted:
- run #2 had one anomalous p99 spike at minute 4; correlate with infra-level preemption log (node heartbeats show transient GC pause). need to rerun with node isolation.
- small number of requests got 503 during early bursts in aggregate-window tests. root cause: our enqueue-buffer overflow threshold too low; bump to 512 or implement spill-to-disk in future.

Next experiments (prio order):
1) add hysteresis to immediate-resume: require quiet period >= 2*hb before fast lane re-enable. rerun hb=10/25 to compare.
2) isolate run on dedicated dev node (no other tenants) to rule out infra noise; reproduce best config (hb=25 agg).
3) test longer bursts (10s) and varying output token lengths (20, 80) to see batch dynamics.
4) instrument per-worker KV-cache metrics and session stickiness to understand hit-rate dip.

Implementation notes / ideas for prod:
- make heartbeat config per-route (low-latency routes: keep hb=10 with higher resources; bursty batch routes: hb=25-50 to save p99).
- expose simple client-side hint header (x-rw-heartbeat: prefer-coalesce) for apps that can tolerate small delay.
- add a lightweight telemetry event when heartbeat delays a request (so product teams can see user-facing latencies introduced).

Quick decision note (for later):
- default server-side policy: "hb=25ms, aggregate-window, enqueue-buffer 512, immediate-resume with 2x hysteresis" as a starting safe default for multi-tenant hosted API.

Loose TODOs (personal):
- write small harness script to vary burst shape programmatically (sin / square / single-impulse).
- capture raw batch size time-series and dump to S3 for plotting (I used local csvs today — move to central).
- sync with Ravi on PR approach for enqueue-buffer bump and add unit tests for drop behavior.

Notes-to-self:
- keep runs reproducible: seed client RNG, store full args in metadata file (date/time, git sha of runtime).
- remind: double-check that quantized model build used the same kernel selection flags as prod (I used -O2 local build, prod uses -O3). kernel differences change latency distribution.

References / where I stored artifacts:
- local csvs: /mnt/devbench/heartbeat-sweep/20251118/*.csv
- flamegraphs + perf reports: s3://dev-artifacts/heartbeat-sweep/20251118

End of scratchpad.
